newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs new maritime law.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs new maritime law.

text.p: President Clinton signed into law Tuesday the Maritime Security Act of 1996 that funds a plan to pay subsidies to U.S.-flag ships for being available to haul defence supplies at wartime.

In a written statement, Clinton said the law "will ensure that the United States will continue to have American flag ships crewed by local American-citizen merchant mariners to meet our nation's economic and sealift defence requirements."

Under the bill, operators of U.S.-flag ships that could be used for military supply purposes would receive $2.3 million a year for each ship this year and $2.1 million a ship for following years through fiscal year 2005. The bill authorised $100 million a year for these payments.

It replaces a current programme that provides government payments to U.S.-flag ship operators based on the difference between the crew and operating costs of U.S.-flag vessels and foreign-flagged ships.
Operating American ships costs more because of higher pay and benefits and more costly regulation.
The new plan would guarantee the Defence Department a pool of American crews and a 47-ship fleet of militarily useful ships, along with the companies' railcars, containers and other facilities.

"The Maritime Security Act will protect American jobs and maintain a U.S. presence in international maritime trade, ensuring that vital imports and exports are delivered in both peacetime and wartime," Clinton said.
"This act reaffirms our nation's resolve to maintain a strong U.S.-flag presence on the high seas for our continued national security and economic growth," he said.

During Senate debate, supporters of the bill said more than 120 U.S.-flag ships were called on to help the U.S. military buildup in the Gulf prior to the Gulf war. At the same time some foreign operators doubled their normal charter rates.
Under the new plan, U.S. shipping firms would have to agree to rates established in advance for chartering in a defence emergency.
